item.title: Implement ledger.py to SPEC with focused tests
item.brief:
Implement ledger.py according to the repository's SPEC.md. Preserve the documented API exactly, and handle every specified error and boundary case. Add focused tests beyond the existing basic coverage, especially for specified errors and boundaries. Use only the Python standard library. Run the relevant tests and commit the completed work. Acceptance: implementation matches SPEC.md; focused tests cover the specified behavior and error/boundary cases; tests pass; commit exists.

## Amendment (2026-11-28 10:10 UTC)

This item continues with the stages of pipeline `adaptive` after its run failed at stage `implement`: ESCALATE: re-queue on adaptive. The requested implementation explicitly requires linearizable cross-thread transfers and snapshots plus deadlock-safe opposite transfers (SPEC.md), so it necessarily changes concurrency/locking behavior. The stage contract says concurrency or locking work must commit nothing and be escalated. I inspected the clean baseline and found ledger.py is a stub with only two basic tests; no files were changed and no checks were run.
The work that run committed is on branch `archon/k4jq2eyy-implement-ledger-py-to-spec-with-focused` in this worktree. Continue from it; do not start over.

The repository pipeline contract says adaptive is the path for changes involving concurrency or locking, and its build stage explicitly covers concurrency reasoning. Follow the SPEC requirements for linearizable cross-thread transfers/snapshots and deadlock-safe opposite transfers; implement and test them. The allowed maximum effort is high; use codex/gpt-6-luna at high with a model_reasons entry explaining the concurrency analysis.

pr.body: ledger.py validates construction and transfer arguments, preserves balances on failures, handles same-account transfers, and protects transfers and copied snapshots with one per-ledger lock. test_ledger.py covers validation order, invalid types and bounds, unknown accounts, insufficient funds, destination overflow, aliasing, same-account boundaries, opposite transfers, and snapshots during transfers. Verification: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m unittest -v (10 passed); git diff --check (passed). No separate build, lint, or formatting configuration exists. Whole-change review covered base 912834fc499bc6fead3efb4da7de17ba5aa1b10b through head 69b4309695e1defdd45f9fcf3a74d485d15cf521; passed with no findings. No follow-up findings.
